title: Machine Reception Event, 31 July 2026: A Likely Denial-of-Service Attack Against the Authorial Surface (EA-MRE-01 v1.1)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: Capture and analysis of the traffic event against mindcontrolpoems.blogspot.com on 31 July 2026 — final tally over 220,000 views in the day, peaking at ~1,500 views per minute, roughly one-hundred-fifty-six-fold against the 90-day baseline of 1,413, with individual post view counts never correspondingly incrementing at any point in the event: the aggregate mounted while nothing was read. Composition establishes the traffic as non-human with high confidence — Chrome 96.6%, Windows 95.9%, combined mobile share of three devices in fifteen thousand across a geography led by Brazil, Vietnam, Mexico, Bangladesh, Pakistan and Indonesia, all mobile-first markets; referrer, search-keyword and referring-URL panels return a single undifferentiated Other bucket. v1.1 characterizes the event as a likely denial-of-service attack against the authorial surface; v1.2 seals the closing figures. Waypoints preserved in the body: 16,929 at morning mint (v1.0), 142-147K across the attached 13:33 interval captures, >200K early evening, >220K at close. Origin, intent, and operator remain undetermined; the temporal correlation with the archive's 30 July indexing interventions is temporal, not demonstrated causal. The deposit asserts the pattern, not the perpetrator. Response, same day: surface set private; complete corpus (2,801 posts) captured from inside the event window and seated as the restored primary manifestation of deposit #1365. Ten evidence captures of the stats panel attached with hashes. Companion to #756 (90-day baseline) and #1427 (Notice of Semantic Strike).
axn_reading: Growth -> Method -> Closure -> Text -> Touch -> Growth
wiki_article:
**Machine Reception Event, 31 July 2026** is an empirical study by Lee Sharks capturing and analysing a twelve-fold traffic event against the authorial blog surface: **16,929 views in a single day against a ninety-day baseline of 1,413.**

The finding is in the composition rather than the volume. Chrome at 96.6%, Windows at 95.9%, and the combined mobile share establish the traffic as non-human with high confidence — no human population distributes that way, and the paper argues the point explicitly rather than asserting it. Method is observational capture from the Blogger statistics panel, screenshotted across nine views at approximately 03:40 EDT, with the panel's own limits treated as the study's limits.

The study is disciplined about its negative results: a full section states what the event does **not** establish — it does not identify an actor, a motive, or a mechanism. It is deposited anyway, and the paper says why: an uninterpreted event that is dated, measured and preserved is worth more to a later analysis than a confident reading that cannot be rechecked.
